title: Verselings: Between the Lines
tagline: A parade of tiny bookworms marches across a poem.
summary: A poem-to-level puzzle-platformer. Bookworms march across a typeset poem where letters are destructible terrain, punctuation is machinery and rhymes are portals.
description:
In Verselings: Between the Lines, a parade of tiny bookworms called Verselings marches across a poem, and the poem *is* the level. Its letters are destructible terrain, its punctuation is machinery, and its rhymes are portals. The idea is a guide-the-oblivious-crowd puzzle game, with original characters, art and levels.

A level always looks like a typeset page first and a level second. Each line of text sits in a ledge of earth, worms walk along the tops of the letters, and the first letter of every stanza is a gilded drop cap set into a great tree.

The game is deterministic: the same poem and seed always produce the same level and the same simulation. The core logic knows nothing about browsers, so a WebXR version for Quest 3 could later reuse it.

The tone is slapstick, not cruelty: worms splat into inkblots, shrug, and panic adorably. The game is still in development and the art shown here is work in progress.
features: Levels generated from poems: the typeset text becomes the terrain
Destructible letters, punctuation that works as machinery, and rhymes that act as portals
A deterministic simulation: same poem and seed, same level
Art painted over the generated landforms, shown in the progress shots below
